cover.headline:
Explain the company.
Then explain the fit.

intro.text: Begin with the customer problem and the company's contribution. Keep this paragraph accessible to a reader who has not seen the investor deck. A partner brief is not a compressed diligence room. This fictional example demonstrates the format; it contains no operating claims.

cover.platformTitle: A clear product. A credible proof point. A reason to partner.

platformBody.text: Describe how the product works in plain language. Separate what is delivered today from what is being demonstrated or developed. Explain the economic or capability unlock without importing an unsupported benchmark from another mission, vessel or market.

tileCaption.text: Image placeholders only. Replace with approved assets and keep provenance and maturity labels visible.

cover.tractionKicker: Evidence that earns the next meeting

tractionNote.text: Every figure needs a date, definition and source. Signed value, pipeline and recognized revenue are different things.

spotlight.title: Keep the product ladder honest.

body.text: Use this panel for the strongest product proof or a concise vessel-family roadmap. Do not let an attractive rendering imply that a future class is already delivered. Unresolved performance claims should be omitted or resolved—not silently relabeled.

spotlight.imageCaption: Abstract placeholder · replace with approved product image

partnership.headline:
A specific partner.
A specific first program.

intro.text: Anchor the case in the partner's actual strategy, capabilities and operating footprint. Explain what the company adds and why the combined offering could create new customer value. Keep proposals distinct from agreements.

body.text: The defined product, technology and customer insight that the partner does not already have.
Source-backed capabilities, relevant manufacturing or channels—not assumed capacity or commitments.

tracks.title: Define the subsystem and the interfaces.

body.text: Distinguish manufacturing an existing design, integrating an available subsystem and co-developing a new system. They have different engineering, commercial and intellectual-property implications.

tracks.value: A clear source of product, service or engineering revenue for the partner.
tracks.start: A short requirements session with named technical owners and a defined decision.

tracks.title: Choose a product and a build package.

body.text: Describe potential production or licensing workshare. Partner facilities and yard relationships are research evidence, not proof of available capacity. Keep the starting request bounded.

tracks.value: A repeatable commercial offering that matches the partner's actual business.
tracks.start: Select a product and nominate the appropriate manufacturing or sourcing team.

tracks.title: Start with an operator and a mission.

body.text: Use marine-specific channel evidence where relevant. Distributor presence does not establish passenger demand, route rights or permits. Prioritize customer discovery rather than a countrywide launch promise.

tracks.value: Additional system and service demand supported by validated customer economics.
tracks.start: One operator, a defined mission and a credible service and validation plan.

expansion.label: Future options:
expansion.text: service support · connected fleet tools · site infrastructure, when the first program supports them.

ask.title: The ask: one sponsor and one scoped evaluation.

body.text: Name the next decision, the people and the required inputs. Sequence requirements, configuration and validation before supply, licensing, investment or construction commitments. Avoid dates or quantities neither party controls.

team.label: Relevant team ·
team.text: Use approved names and roles; do not import another partner's contacts.
